end.summary:
• Myra copied shapes on a grid by counting gaps between dots; this was shown on a new question.
• Myra recognised that turning or moving a shape keeps its size and shape; this was shown on new questions.
• Myra practised continuing tile patterns and identified that the next group starts with red; a why or new-situation question is still needed.
• Myra was unsure on some new questions, including one about a rotated shape’s appearance; later they stated that turning does not change the number of squares and swaps length and width.
end.parentNote: Myra practised copying shapes by counting the gaps between dots, and recognised that turning a shape does not change its size or number of squares. They were unsure on some new questions, including why a diamond can look longer, but later used the idea that turning swaps length and width. At home, draw a few shapes on squared paper and ask Myra to copy one, turn it, and explain what stays the same; continue a short tile pattern and ask what rule is being used.
